solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: City university in Zambia originally having money to burn?

indicators.note: originally means only the opening letter of the word Zambia is used

parts.note: someone with money to burn is rich

explanation.surface: A query about a Zambian university town whose students are flush with cash.
explanation.walkthrough: Z (Zambia's first letter) is followed by U and RICH; 'in' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Zurich is the largest Swiss city, so it is an example of a city.

clue.text: Unknown European group infiltrated by a fanatic

indicators.note: infiltrated by means a piece gets inside the others

parts.note: Z is a mathematical unknown
a lot is a group, as at an auction

explanation.surface: A mysterious European group has been infiltrated by an extremist.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes inside ZELOT, between the E and the L.
explanation.definitionFit: A zealot is someone fanatical in pursuing a cause, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Contrite worker who's been confined again?

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
pent, as in pent up, means confined
an ant is the classic worker insect

explanation.surface: A sorry workman who has been locked up for a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads RE-PENT ANT, an ant penned in again; the question mark flags this playful split.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone repentant feels sorrow for wrongdoing, which is what contrite means.

clue.text: Native American in hired vehicle touring Rhode Island

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the vehicle's letters surround the state

parts.note: a cab is a vehicle hired for a journey
RI is the postal abbreviation for Rhode Island

explanation.surface: A Native American takes a taxi tour of Rhode Island.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caribs are an indigenous people of the Caribbean and northern South America.

clue.text: Clairvoyant visited by Saint David, most famously

indicators.note: being visited by someone means having them come inside, so one letter goes into the other word

parts.note: a palmist claims to foresee the future by reading hands

explanation.surface: A fortune-teller receives a call from Wales's patron saint, the most famous visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saint David' reads as one person, but Saint gives S and David is the definition: King David is traditionally the author of the Psalms.
explanation.definitionFit: King David is credited with writing many of the biblical Psalms, so he is the best-known example of a psalm writer.

clue.text: Soft-hearted type's feeling about first of many top people?

indicators.note: about means the word for feeling goes round the letter

parts.note: sentient means capable of feeling

indicators.note: first of means only the opening letter of many is used

parts.note: the A-list is the top tier of celebrities

explanation.surface: A sentimental person feels for the first among many elite people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the feeling word round M; the A-list is the top tier of celebrities, and the 's is a link meaning is.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentimentalist indulges in tender emotion, a soft-hearted person.

clue.text: Vessel dropping off a US magazine in midday break

indicators.note: dropping off means a letter is shed from the word

parts.note: a launch is a type of boat
Time is a US news magazine

explanation.surface: A boat drops off an American magazine during the lunch break.
explanation.walkthrough: LAUNCH loses its A to give LUNCH, then TIME is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunchtime is the break in the middle of the day for a meal.

clue.text: Girl regularly leaves tough meat, finding fibre

indicators.note: leaves means those letters depart from the word, leaving the rest

parts.note: gristle is tough cartilage in meat

indicators.note: regularly means alternate letters of girl are taken

explanation.surface: A girl often leaves her chewy meat and eats fibre instead.
explanation.walkthrough: GR (the first and third letters of Girl) leaves GRISTLE. Istle is a plant fibre from agave, used for cord and brushes.
explanation.definitionFit: Istle is a coarse vegetable fibre obtained from Mexican agave and yucca plants.

clue.text: Time to restore confidence to a son missing love?

indicators.note: missing means one letter is absent from the word

parts.note: to reassure someone is to restore their confidence
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Is it time to reassure a son who misses his love?
explanation.walkthrough: 'love' reads as part of what the son is missing, but it is the definition; one S is dropped from REASSURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasure is an affectionate term for a beloved person, much like calling someone love.

clue.text: Enjoying realised ambition, having led with merit at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A naval commander fulfils his dream after leading his crew with distinction.
explanation.walkthrough: HAVING, LED and MERIT are rearranged; 'with' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Living the dream is an idiom for enjoying the life you always hoped for.

clue.text: A second individual torn apart by current slur

indicators.note: a word torn apart by another has that other piece pushed into its middle

parts.note: an individual is a person
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Someone is ripped apart by a slur doing the rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like an adjective meaning topical, but it is I, the symbol for electric current, which splits PERSON into PERS-I-ON.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast aspersions is to make damaging remarks, so an aspersion is a slur on someone's character.

clue.text: Explosive material in container brought back by sappers

indicators.note: brought back means the word for the container is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a tin is a container
RE, the Royal Engineers, are the British Army's sappers

explanation.surface: Explosives are packed into a canister which army engineers bring back.
explanation.walkthrough: Sappers are military engineers; in crosswords they are RE, the Royal Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitre, or saltpetre, is potassium nitrate, a key ingredient of gunpowder.

clue.text: Keep wife in cricket side

indicators.note: in means the letter for wife goes inside the word for the cricket side

parts.note: the on side is one half of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A man keeps his wife in the cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is split into the off side and the on (leg) side, so a side can be ON.
explanation.definitionFit: To own something is to possess it, which is to keep it as yours.

clue.text: Extremely brazen, his sister's cultivated national identity

indicators.note: land that is cultivated is worked over, so these letters are dug up and rearranged
extremely means only the outermost letters of brazen are taken

parts.note: the word sister supplies the letters; the 's stands for is, a link

explanation.surface: A brazen sister affects a cultivated air of being thoroughly British.
explanation.walkthrough: BN (the ends of brazen) is added to HIS and SISTER and the lot rearranged; 'cultivated' looks like praise for the sister but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Britishness is the quality of being British, the national character of the UK.

clue.text: Chatting with judge in flight?

parts.note: awing is an old word meaning on the wing, in flight

explanation.surface: A judge chats away while airborne.
explanation.walkthrough: AWING is a rare form meaning on the wing; the question mark flags the unusual word.
explanation.definitionFit: To jaw is informal for to talk at length, so jawing is chatting.

clue.text: National idioms a woman found going over a chap's manuscript

parts.note: Iris is a woman's name
his means belonging to a chap

explanation.surface: A woman looks over a man's manuscript for local turns of phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Irishisms are expressions characteristic of Irish English, idioms of one nation.

clue.text: One who gives out marks missing in term-time mix-up

indicators.note: a mix-up jumbles things, so the remaining letters are rearranged
missing means one letter is taken out of the phrase

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for marks, the former German currency

explanation.surface: A teacher hands out marks, though some go missing in a muddle during term.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing M from TERMTIME leaves TERTIME, which is then rearranged; 'gives out marks' looks like the surface, but marks belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An emitter is something that sends out signals, light or particles, literally one that gives them out.

clue.text: Like some fat Tudor composer keeping old wife and horse

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the composer's name holds the other letters

parts.note: Thomas Tallis was an English composer of the Tudor period
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: An overweight Tudor musician looks after an aged wife and a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horse' is slang for heroin, which gives H.
explanation.definitionFit: Tallow is rendered animal fat, so tallowish means resembling some kinds of fat.

clue.text: Slovenly hotel dejected chums are upset over

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the letters read in reverse

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
dejected means sad
chums are pals

explanation.surface: Sad pals are upset about a scruffy hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: HSADPALS reversed gives SLAP-DAS-H.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapdash work is careless and hasty, the sense of slovenly.

clue.text: Latvian allows husband to pen note

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so the musical note goes inside the other letters

parts.note: allows means lets
ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A Latvian woman lets her husband write a note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' suggests writing, but here it means to shut in: TI goes inside LETSH.
explanation.definitionFit: Lettish is an older name for the Latvian language, spoken by the Letts.

clue.text: Choirboy to shake with fear, having missed Mass

indicators.note: having missed means one letter is left out of the word

parts.note: to tremble is to shake with fear
M is the abbreviation for mass in physics

explanation.surface: A choirboy quakes with fright after missing the church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' looks like the church service, but it gives M, the scientific abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A treble is a boy singer with a high voice, the usual role of a choirboy.

clue.text: Attempt to divide open tart and a measure of wine

indicators.note: to divide means the attempt splits the tart into two parts

parts.note: a flan is an open pastry case with a filling
a go is an attempt

explanation.surface: Someone tries to cut a tart in half while serving wine.
explanation.walkthrough: A flan is an open pastry case, which is why 'open tart' is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagon is a large vessel for wine, and by extension the quantity it holds.

clue.text: Mind food shop, taking first of compounds like LSD?

parts.note: the psyche is the mind
a deli is a delicatessen, a food shop

indicators.note: first of means only the opening letter of compounds is used

explanation.surface: A warning to look after a food shop that has started stocking drug compounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mind' reads as a verb, but it is a noun giving PSYCHE.
explanation.definitionFit: LSD is the classic hallucinogen, and psychedelic describes drugs that produce such altered perceptions.

clue.text: Long story about Eeyore, primarily

indicators.note: about means the story's letters surround the other letter

parts.note: a yarn is a story

indicators.note: primarily means only the first letter of Eeyore is used

explanation.surface: A lengthy tale about the gloomy donkey from Winnie-the-Pooh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective describing the story, but it is the verb meaning yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to yearn for it.

clue.text: Wary when star of US gangster movies drops in at last

indicators.note: drops means a letter is let go from the star's name

parts.note: James Cagney starred in classic Hollywood gangster films

indicators.note: at last means the final letter of in is taken

explanation.surface: A cautious film star finally drops in on a visit.
explanation.walkthrough: CAGNEY loses N, the last letter of 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cagey means being guarded and cautious, reluctant to give information away.

clue.text: See about providing shelter for western bird

indicators.note: providing shelter for means one piece encloses the other
about means the word for see is turned round

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or look

explanation.surface: An instruction to arrange cover for a bird from the west.
explanation.walkthrough: LO reversed gives OL, which takes W inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An owl is a nocturnal bird of prey, so it is an example of a bird.

clue.text: Gather in a New England state, briefly

parts.note: Mass is the short form of Massachusetts, a New England state

explanation.surface: People gather in a state in north-east America for a short while.
explanation.walkthrough: New England is the north-eastern corner of the US; Massachusetts is shortened to MASS.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to gather or collect a quantity of something.

clue.text: Relaxed midshipman, one captivated by medal

parts.note: Mr Midshipman Easy is the title hero of Captain Marryat's naval novel

indicators.note: captivated by means held captive inside, so one letter sits within the other word

parts.note: gong is British slang for a medal
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A junior naval officer is relaxed, having been charmed by a medal.
explanation.walkthrough: The literary allusion is to Marryat's 1836 novel Mr Midshipman Easy; GONG is British slang for a medal or award.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone easygoing is relaxed and tolerant, not easily upset.

clue.text: Generous with funds ultimately invested in refuge, perhaps

indicators.note: invested in plays on money: the letters are put inside the word for the refuge

parts.note: a home is one example of a refuge
and can mean with, as in bread and butter

indicators.note: ultimately means only the last letter of funds is used

explanation.surface: A generous donation with funds put into a shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested' looks financial alongside funds, but it means placed inside: ANDS goes into HOME.
explanation.definitionFit: A handsome sum or gift is a large, generous one.

clue.text: Some unhealthy phenomenon that's in centre of Guinea-Bissau

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some unhealthy trend has struck the heart of a West African country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre of Guinea-Bissau' sounds like a place, but the definition describes the punctuation mark joining Guinea and Bissau.
explanation.definitionFit: The country's name is written with a dash linking its two halves, so that punctuation mark sits right in the middle.
